description: WIRES meaning-inference (domains/meaning_inference.py + seeds/meaning_inference.json) into the real comprehension pipeline as a `meaning_inference` AnalysisStage (seeds/literary_analysis_driving.json's la_dispatch_* / AnalysisStage / Cortex machinery, unmodified). read_and_comprehend's own ~24 read_clause calls per sentence pair are ALWAYS write=False (its own decomposition machinery), so the five meaning-inference sources (selectional/definition/morphology/analogy/in-situ construction) never fired through it before this seed -- only a DIRECT read_clause(agent, sentence, write=True) call fires them. This rule's DECISION is graph-native: dispatch the 'meaning_inference' stage once the flow's own SentenceParse nodes exist (the spine is done -- there is text to re-read) AND the 'monitoring' stage (the last GUARANTEED-to-complete comprehension stage -- gated only on Count(SmEntity)>0, same precondition as infer_goal/discourse, empirically reached 'done' even for texts with no SmEvent/DiscourseEvent, e.g. a bare copular definition) has itself reached 'done'. This deliberately excludes the OPTIONAL, material-triggered order-N stages ('narrative'/'trope', gated on Count(SmEvent)/Count(NarrativeRole) > 0) as a precondition -- those can legitimately stay 'pending' forever for a non-narrative text (verified empirically: 'A glimt is a lake.' never mints an SmEvent), so requiring them would deadlock this stage for exactly the definitional/analogy test sentences meaning-inference itself targets. Waiting on 'monitoring' still guarantees this stage runs AFTER every stage that reads predication/entity graph state (spine, infer_goal, discourse, infer_causal, enabling, centrality, tom, monitoring), so its purely-additive Concept/Predication/PredicationSlot/InferredSense/AffixCandidate/ConceptSignature writes (verified: no SmEntity/SmEvent/DiscourseEvent/NarrativeRole/Trope/Claim node is ever touched) can never perturb an earlier stage's already-computed output -- the comprehension report is byte-identical with/without this stage. The mechanical re-read itself (one read_clause(agent, sentence, write=True) call per SentenceParse) is domains/reading_drive.py's `_shim_meaning_inference` -- a thin boundary invocation, the SAME shape as every other stage shim; the fold/mint/combine/abstain/supersede decision for the inferred senses themselves lives entirely in seeds/meaning_inference.json's rules, loaded automatically (idempotent) by the annotators read_clause(write=True) already calls.

microtheory.name: meaning_inference_stage
microtheory.description: a standing rule that dispatches the meaning_inference comprehension stage once the spine is done and the last guaranteed-to-complete comprehension stage (monitoring) has finished, so a re-read for meaning-inference purposes runs late and cannot perturb any earlier stage's output.

rules.name: la_dispatch_meaning_inference
rules.comment: Fire the 'meaning_inference' faculty stage once the flow's own SentenceParse nodes exist (spine done -- there is text to re-read) AND the 'monitoring' stage has reached 'done' (the last comprehension stage GUARANTEED to complete, so meaning_inference always runs LAST, after every stage that reads graph state -- see this seed's description for why 'narrative'/'trope' are deliberately NOT gated on). The DECISION-to-fire + the ORDER are this where-clause, evaluated by run_rules -- never a Python faculty sequence.
